minimal_trustworthy_remedy.kind: generic preserved-source span remap with duplicate aliases
steps: Keep saved upstream files byte-for-byte; record all raw hashes and both source IDs as provenance aliases of one canonical combined-range English body.
For each source component, record target Pali document/key or explicit shared-formula, abbreviation, reference, or untranslated relationship. Do not infer equivalence from source filename alone.

Derive narrower display/alignment views from those source spans, or expose a combined-range view with both original Pali documents. Store shared English only once canonically; a shared displayed prefix must reference that source span instead of inventing English.
Preserve English token order inside the canonical source. Cross-document references can expose the component Pali keys, while ordinary monotonic cuts apply only within valid local spans.

Validate source-token conservation once per canonical range, duplicate alias identity, full component coverage, and zero literal variant-to-wrong-faculty/path mappings. Exclude untranslated structural metadata and source abbreviations from literal coverage counts.
minimal_trustworthy_remedy.immediate_limit_statement: Current trial remains truthful only if these records are treated as unresolved source-scope limitations. Passing/not-found boundary status does not establish correct per-key correlation for these source ranges.

why_cuts_alone_cannot_solve: Each of two narrower Pali documents currently receives the whole same combined-range English body. Range keys lack the literal terminal-attention discourse; terminal-single keys lack the earlier variants (and SN45.62 lacks dawn). A cut can partition the current body monotonically but cannot move foreign words to another Pali document, represent shared spans, or deduplicate the two source copies. Correcting only one copy leaves the other copy foreign or forces loss/rewrite of preserved source.
changes_made: Only this scratch assessment JSON; no source, translation, cut, script, app, or Git changes.
